-- Precondition auxiliary definitions
-- No auxiliary definitions needed for precondition

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def set_precond (str : String) (pos : String.Pos) (char : Char) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition
def set_function (str : String) (pos : String.Pos) (char : Char) : String :=
  String.set str pos char

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
-- Auxiliary definition to check if a position is valid in a string
def String.validPos (s : String) (pos : String.Pos) : Prop :=
  pos < s.endPos

-- Auxiliary definition to check if a character is 7-bit ASCII
def Char.is7BitASCII (c : Char) : Prop :=
  c.val < 128

-- Auxiliary definition to check if a string contains only 7-bit ASCII characters
def String.is7BitASCII (s : String) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : String.Pos), i < s.endPos → (s.get i).is7BitASCII

-- Helper function to describe the result when position is valid
def String.modifiedAt (s : String) (pos : String.Pos) (c : Char) : String :=
  if h : pos < s.endPos then
    s.set pos c
  else
    s

  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  -- If position is valid, character at position is replaced
  -- If position is invalid, string is returned unchanged

    result.get pos = char ∧

    (∀ (i : String.Pos), i < str.endPos → (i = pos ∨ result.get i = str.get i)) ∧

    result.length = str.length)

problem_description:
Splits a string at each character for which `p` returns `true`.

The characters that satisfy `p` are not included in any of the resulting strings. If multiple
characters in a row satisfy `p`, then the resulting list will contain empty strings.

Examples:
* `"coffee tea water".split (·.isWhitespace) = ["coffee", "tea", "water"]`
* `"coffee  tea  water".split (·.isWhitespace) = ["coffee", "", "tea", "", "water"]`
* `"fun x =>\n  x + 1\n".split (· == '\n') = ["fun x =>", "  x + 1", ""]`
formal_problem:
import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.split_precond (s : String) (p : Char → Bool) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition
def String.split_impl (s : String) (p : Char → Bool) (h_precond : String.split_precond s p) : List String :=
  s.split p

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
inductive SplitState : Type where
  | inWord (acc : String) : SplitState
  | afterSeparator : SplitState

def processChar (state : SplitState) (c : Char) (p : Char → Bool) : SplitState × Option String :=
  if p c then
    match state with
    | SplitState.inWord acc => (SplitState.afterSeparator, if acc.isEmpty then none else some acc)
    | SplitState.afterSeparator => (SplitState.afterSeparator, none)
  else
    match state with
    | SplitState.inWord acc => (SplitState.inWord (acc.push c), none)
    | SplitState.afterSeparator => (SplitState.inWord (String.singleton c), none)

def finalizeSplit (state : SplitState) : Option String :=
  match state with
  | SplitState.inWord acc => if acc.isEmpty then none else some acc
  | SplitState.afterSeparator => none

def expectedSplit (s : String) (p : Char → Bool) : List String :=
  let initState : SplitState := SplitState.afterSeparator
  let (finalState, results) := s.foldl (λ (state_result : SplitState × List String) c => 
    let (state, results) := state_result
    let (newState, maybeStr) := processChar state c p
    (newState, match maybeStr with | some str => results ++ [str] | none => results)) (initState, [])
  match finalizeSplit finalState with
  | some str => results ++ [str]
  | none => results

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.split_postcond (s : String) (p : Char → Bool) (result: List String) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  result = expectedSplit s p
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- Proof content
theorem String.split_postcond_satisfied (s: String) (p: Char → Bool) (h_precond : String.split_precond s p) :
    String.split_postcond s p (String.split_impl s p h_precond) := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

inductive SplitState : Type where
  | inWord (acc : String) : SplitState
  | afterSeparator : SplitState

def processChar (state : SplitState) (c : Char) (p : Char → Bool) : SplitState × Option String :=
  if p c then
    match state with
    | SplitState.inWord acc => (SplitState.afterSeparator, if acc.isEmpty then none else some acc)
    | SplitState.afterSeparator => (SplitState.afterSeparator, none)
  else
    match state with
    | SplitState.inWord acc => (SplitState.inWord (acc.push c), none)
    | SplitState.afterSeparator => (SplitState.inWord (String.singleton c), none)

def finalizeSplit (state : SplitState) : Option String :=
  match state with
  | SplitState.inWord acc => if acc.isEmpty then none else some acc
  | SplitState.afterSeparator => none

def expectedSplit (s : String) (p : Char → Bool) : List String :=
  let initState : SplitState := SplitState.afterSeparator
  let (finalState, results) := s.foldl (λ (state_result : SplitState × List String) c => 
    let (state, results) := state_result
    let (newState, maybeStr) := processChar state c p
    (newState, match maybeStr with | some str => results ++ [str] | none => results)) (initState, [])
  match finalizeSplit finalState with
  | some str => results ++ [str]
  | none => results

problem_description:
If `pre` is a prefix of `s`, returns the remainder. Returns `s` unmodified otherwise.

The string `pre` is a prefix of `s` if there exists a `t : String` such that `s = pre ++ t`. If so,
the result is `t`. Otherwise, it is `s`.

Use `String.dropPrefix?` to return `none` when `pre` is not a prefix.

Examples:
 * `"red green blue".stripPrefix "red " = "green blue"`
 * `"red green blue".stripPrefix "reed " = "red green blue"`

problem_description:
Checks whether substrings of two strings are equal. Substrings are indicated by their starting
positions and a size in _UTF-8 bytes_. Returns `false` if the indicated substring does not exist in
either string.

import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.substrEq_precond (s1 : String) (pos1 : String.Pos) (s2 : String) (pos2 : String.Pos) (size : Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  let valid_pos1 := pos1 ≤ s1.endPos
  let valid_pos2 := pos2 ≤ s2.endPos
  valid_pos1 ∧ valid_pos2
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition
#check String.substrEq

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
def String.validSubstringAt (s : String) (pos : String.Pos) (size : Nat) : Prop :=
  let endPos := pos.1 + size
  endPos ≤ s.endPos.1

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.substrEq_postcond (s1 : String) (pos1 : String.Pos) (s2 : String) (pos2 : String.Pos) (size : Nat) (result: Bool) (h_precond : String.substrEq_precond (s1) (pos1) (s2) (pos2) (size)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  let substring1_valid := String.validSubstringAt s1 pos1 size
  let substring2_valid := String.validSubstringAt s2 pos2 size
  
  if result then
    substring1_valid ∧ substring2_valid ∧
    s1.extract pos1 { byteIdx := pos1.1 + size } = s2.extract pos2 { byteIdx := pos2.1 + size }
  else
    ¬substring1_valid ∨ ¬substring2_valid ∨
    s1.extract pos1 { byteIdx := pos1.1 + size } ≠ s2.extract pos2 { byteIdx := pos2.1 + size }
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

  let valid_pos2 := pos2 ≤ s2.endPos
  valid_pos1 ∧ valid_pos2

problem_description:
Creates a new string that contains the longest prefix of `s` in which `p` returns `true` for all
characters.

Examples:
* `"red green blue".takeWhile (·.isLetter) = "red"`
* `"red green blue".takeWhile (· == 'r') = "r"`
* `"red green blue".takeWhile (· != 'n') = "red gree"`
* `"red green blue".takeWhile (fun _ => true) = "red green blue"`
formal_problem:
import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.takeWhile_precond (s : String) (p : Char → Bool) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition
-- String.takeWhile

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
-- Helper function to check if all characters in a string satisfy a predicate
def String.all_chars (s : String) (p : Char → Bool) : Bool :=
  s.data.all p

-- Helper function to check if a string is a prefix of another string
def String.isPrefix (pre : String) (s : String) : Prop :=
  pre.data = (s.data.take pre.length)

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.takeWhile_postcond (s : String) (p : Char → Bool) (result: String) (h_precond : String.takeWhile_precond s p) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  -- The result is a prefix of the input string
    String.isPrefix result s ∧
    -- All characters in the result satisfy the predicate p
    result.all_chars p = true ∧
    -- The result is the longest such prefix: either it equals s, or the next character doesn't satisfy p
    (result.length = s.length ∨ 
     (result.length < s.length ∧ 
      p (s.data.get! result.length) = false))
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

problem_description:
Converts a string to a pretty-printer document, replacing newlines in the string with
`Std.Format.line`.
formal_problem:
import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.toFormat_precond (s : String) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition
-- String.toFormat

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
-- Helper function to check if a Format represents a line break
def Format.isLine : Std.Format → Bool
  | Std.Format.line => true
  | _ => false

-- Helper function to split a string by newlines and convert to list of Format pieces
def String.splitNewlines (s : String) : List String :=
  s.split (· = '\n')

-- Helper to check if the result format correctly represents the string with newlines replaced by Format.line
def Format.representsStringWithLines (f : Std.Format) (s : String) : Prop :=
  -- The format should be equivalent to joining the split parts with Format.line
  -- When the string contains no newlines, it should be a text format
  -- When it contains newlines, parts should be separated by line breaks
  if s.contains '\n' then
    -- The format represents the string with newlines replaced by Format.line
    ∃ (parts : List String), 
      parts = s.splitNewlines ∧ 
      parts.length > 0
  else
    -- No newlines, so it should just be the string as text
    True

  -- !benchmark @start postcond

    Format.representsStringWithLines result s ∧
    -- If string is empty, result should represent empty format
    (s = "" → result = Std.Format.nil ∨ result = Std.Format.text "") ∧
    -- If string has no newlines, it should be represented as text
    (¬s.contains '\n' → ∃ (t : String), t = s)

problem_description:
Interprets a string as the decimal representation of an integer, returning it. Returns `none` if
the string does not contain a decimal integer.

A string can be interpreted as a decimal integer if it only consists of at least one decimal digit
and optionally `-` in front. Leading `+` characters are not allowed.

Use `String.isInt` to check whether `String.toInt?` would return `some`. `String.toInt!` is an
alternative that panics instead of returning `none` when the string is not an integer.

Examples:
 * `"".toInt? = none`
 * `"-".toInt? = none`
 * `"0".toInt? = some 0`
 * `"5".toInt? = some 5`
 * `"-5".toInt? = some (-5)`
 * `"587".toInt? = some 587`
 * `"-587".toInt? = some (-587)`
 * `" 5".toInt? = none`
 * `"2-3".toInt? = none`
 * `"0xff".toInt? = none`
formal_problem:
import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def toInt?_precond (s : String) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition
def toInt? (s : String) (h_precond : toInt?_precond s) : Option Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start impl
  match s with
  | "" => none
  | s' => 
      if s'.toList.all (λ c => c.isDigit) ∧ s' ≠ "" then
        some (s'.foldl (λ acc c => acc * 10 + (c.toNat - '0'.toNat)) 0)
      else if s'.startsWith "-" ∧ s'.length > 1 ∧ (s'.drop 1).toList.all (λ c => c.isDigit) then
        some (-((s'.drop 1).foldl (λ acc c => acc * 10 + (c.toNat - '0'.toNat)) 0))
      else
        none
  -- !benchmark @end impl

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
def isDecimalInt (s : String) : Prop :=
  (s = "" → False) ∧
  (s.toList = [] → False) ∧
  (match s.toList with
   | [] => False
   | ['-'] => False
   | '-' :: cs => cs.all (λ c => c.isDigit) ∧ cs ≠ []

problem_description:
Removes leading and trailing whitespace from a string.

“Whitespace” is defined as characters for which `Char.isWhitespace` returns `true`.

Examples:
* `"abc".trim = "abc"`
* `"   abc".trim = "abc"`
* `"abc \t  ".trim = "abc"`
* `"  abc   ".trim = "abc"`
* `"abc\ndef\n".trim = "abc\ndef"`
formal_problem:
import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.trim_precond (s : String) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition
#check String.trim

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
-- Helper function to check if a character is whitespace
def is_whitespace (c : Char) : Bool := c.isWhitespace

-- Helper function to find the first non-whitespace character index from the left
def first_non_ws (s : String) : Nat :=
  let chars := s.toList
  let rec find_first (cs : List Char) (idx : Nat) : Nat :=
    match cs with
    | [] => idx
    | c :: rest => if is_whitespace c then find_first rest (idx + 1) else idx
  find_first chars 0

-- Helper function to find the last non-whitespace character index from the right
def last_non_ws (s : String) : Nat :=
  let chars := s.toList
  let len := chars.length
  let rec find_last (cs : List Char) (idx : Nat) : Nat :=
    match cs with
    | [] => 0
    | c :: rest => 
      let rest_result := find_last rest (idx + 1)
      if is_whitespace c then rest_result else idx + 1
  find_last chars 0

-- Check if all characters in a string are whitespace
def all_whitespace (s : String) : Bool :=
  s.toList.all is_whitespace

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.trim_postcond (s : String) (result: String) (h_precond : String.trim_precond s) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  -- The result has no leading or trailing whitespace
    (∀ i : Nat, i < result.length → 
      (i = 0 → ¬is_whitespace result.toList[i]!) ∧
      (i = result.length - 1 → result.length > 0 → ¬is_whitespace result.toList[i]!)) ∧
    -- The result is a substring of the original string
    (∃ start_idx end_idx : Nat, 
      start_idx ≤ end_idx ∧ 
      end_idx ≤ s.length ∧
      result = (s.toList.drop start_idx |>.take (end_idx - start_idx)).asString) ∧
    -- If the original string is all whitespace, result is empty
    (all_whitespace s → result = "") ∧
    -- If the original string has no leading/trailing whitespace, result equals original
    ((s.length > 0 ∧ ¬is_whitespace s.toList[0]! ∧ ¬is_whitespace s.toList[s.length - 1]!) → result = s) ∧
    -- The result preserves all non-whitespace characters and internal whitespace from the original
    (∀ i j : Nat, i < s.length → j < s.length → i < j →
      ¬is_whitespace s.toList[i]! → ¬is_whitespace s.toList[j]! →
      ∃ i' j' : Nat, i' < result.length ∧ j' < result.length ∧ i' < j' ∧
        result.toList[i']! = s.toList[i]! ∧ result.toList[j']! = s.toList[j]! ∧
        (j - i = j' - i' ∨ (∃ k : Nat, i < k ∧ k < j ∧ is_whitespace s.toList[k]!)))
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- Proof content
theorem String.trim_postcond_satisfied (s: String) (h_precond : String.trim_precond s) :
    String.trim_postcond s (s.trim) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

    match cs with
    | [] => idx
    | c :: rest => if is_whitespace c then find_first rest (idx + 1) else idx

problem_description:
Computes the position of the Unicode codepoint at UTF-16 offset
`utf16pos` in the substring of `s` starting at UTF-8 offset `off`.
formal_problem:
import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.utf16PosToCodepointPosFrom_precond (s : String) (utf16pos : Nat) (off : String.Pos) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  -- The offset must be a valid position in the string
  off.byteIdx ≤ s.endPos.byteIdx
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition
-- String.utf16PosToCodepointPosFrom

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
-- Helper function to count UTF-16 code units from a position
def String.countUtf16From (s : String) (start : String.Pos) (cpCount : Nat) : Nat :=
  let rec loop (pos : String.Pos) (remaining : Nat) (utf16Count : Nat) : Nat :=
    if remaining = 0 then utf16Count
    else if pos.byteIdx ≥ s.endPos.byteIdx then utf16Count
    else
      let c := s.get pos
      let nextPos := s.next pos
      let utf16Size := if c.val ≤ 0xFFFF then 1 else 2
      loop nextPos (remaining - 1) (utf16Count + utf16Size)
  loop start cpCount 0

-- Helper function to check if a codepoint count corresponds to a UTF-16 position

index `i` is out of bounds or is not the start of a valid UTF-8 character.
formal_problem:
import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def utf8DecodeChar?_precond (bytes : ByteArray) (i : Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  i < bytes.size
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition

  -- Implementation would go here
  none

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
def isValidUTF8Start (bytes : ByteArray) (i : Nat) : Bool :=
  let b0 := bytes[i]!
  if b0 < 0x80 then
    true
  else if b0 < 0xC0 then
    false
  else if b0 < 0xE0 then
    i + 1 < bytes.size && (bytes[i + 1]! &&& 0xC0) == 0x80
  else if b0 < 0xF0 then
    i + 2 < bytes.size && (bytes[i + 1]! &&& 0xC0) == 0x80 && (bytes[i + 2]! &&& 0xC0) == 0x80
  else if b0 < 0xF8 then
    i + 3 < bytes.size && (bytes[i + 1]! &&& 0xC0) == 0x80 && (bytes[i + 2]! &&& 0xC0) == 0x80 && (bytes[i + 3]! &&& 0xC0) == 0x80
  else

  let b0 := bytes[i]!
  if b0 < 0x80 then
    some (Char.ofNat b0.toNat)
  else if b0 < 0xE0 then
    let b1 := bytes[i + 1]!
    let codepoint := ((b0.toNat &&& 0x1F) <<< 6) ||| (b1.toNat &&& 0x3F)
    if codepoint >= 0x80 then some (Char.ofNat codepoint) else none
  else if b0 < 0xF0 then
    let b1 := bytes[i + 1]!
    let b2 := bytes[i + 2]!
    let codepoint := ((b0.toNat &&& 0x0F) <<< 12) ||| ((b1.toNat &&& 0x3F) <<< 6) ||| (b2.toNat &&& 0x3F)
    if codepoint >= 0x800 && ¬(codepoint >= 0xD800 ∧ codepoint < 0xE000) then some (Char.ofNat codepoint) else none
  else if b0 < 0xF8 then
    let b1 := bytes[i + 1]!
    let b2 := bytes[i + 2]!
    let b3 := bytes[i + 3]!
    let codepoint := ((b0.toNat &&& 0x07) <<< 18) ||| ((b1.toNat &&& 0x3F) <<< 12) ||| ((b2.toNat &&& 0x3F) <<< 6) ||| (b3.toNat &&& 0x3F)

problem_description: Returns the sequence of bytes in a character's UTF-8 encoding.
formal_problem:
import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.utf8EncodeChar_precond (c : Char) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition
-- String.utf8EncodeChar

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
-- Helper function to compute UTF-8 encoding length based on codepoint value
def utf8EncodingLength (c : Char) : Nat :=
  let val := c.val
  if val < 0x80 then 1
  else if val < 0x800 then 2
  else if val < 0x10000 then 3
  else 4

-- Helper function to check if a byte is a valid UTF-8 continuation byte (10xxxxxx)
def isUTF8ContinuationByte (b : UInt8) : Prop :=
  (b &&& 0xC0) = 0x80

-- Helper function to decode UTF-8 bytes back to codepoint value
def decodeUTF8Bytes (bytes : List UInt8) : Option UInt32 :=
  match bytes with
  | [b1] => 
      if b1 < 0x80 then some b1.toUInt32 else none
  | [b1, b2] =>
      if (b1 &&& 0xE0) = 0xC0 && (b2 &&& 0xC0) = 0x80 then
        some (((b1 &&& 0x1F).toUInt32 <<< 6) ||| (b2 &&& 0x3F).toUInt32)
      else none
  | [b1, b2, b3] =>
      if (b1 &&& 0xF0) = 0xE0 && (b2 &&& 0xC0) = 0x80 && (b3 &&& 0xC0) = 0x80 then
        some (((b1 &&& 0x0F).toUInt32 <<< 12) ||| ((b2 &&& 0x3F).toUInt32 <<< 6) ||| (b3 &&& 0x3F).toUInt32)
      else none
  | [b1, b2, b3, b4] =>
      if (b1 &&& 0xF8) = 0xF0 && (b2 &&& 0xC0) = 0x80 && (b3 &&& 0xC0) = 0x80 && (b4 &&& 0xC0) = 0x80 then
        some (((b1 &&& 0x07).toUInt32 <<< 18) ||| ((b2 &&& 0x3F).toUInt32 <<< 12) ||| ((b3 &&& 0x3F).toUInt32 <<< 6) ||| (b4 &&& 0x3F).toUInt32)
      else none
  | _ => none

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.utf8EncodeChar_postcond (c : Char) (result: List UInt8) (h_precond : String.utf8EncodeChar_precond c) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  -- The result is non-empty and has the correct length
    result.length = utf8EncodingLength c ∧
    -- The result correctly encodes the character
    decodeUTF8Bytes result = some c.val ∧
    -- All bytes are valid (non-zero for well-formedness)
    result ≠ [] ∧
    -- The encoding follows UTF-8 structure
    (match result with
     | [b1] => b1 < 0x80  -- Single byte: 0xxxxxxx

     | [b1, b2, b3] => (b1 &&& 0xF0) = 0xE0 ∧ isUTF8ContinuationByte b2 ∧ isUTF8ContinuationByte b3  -- Three bytes
     | [b1, b2, b3, b4] => (b1 &&& 0xF8) = 0xF0 ∧ isUTF8ContinuationByte b2 ∧ isUTF8ContinuationByte b3 ∧ isUTF8ContinuationByte b4  -- Four bytes
     | _ => False)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

problem_description: Checks whether an array of bytes is a valid UTF-8 encoding of a string.
formal_problem:
import Mathlib

-- Precondition auxiliary definitions
inductive UTF8Byte : Type
  | ascii (b : UInt8) : UTF8Byte
  | continuation (b : UInt8) : UTF8Byte
  | two_byte_lead (b : UInt8) : UTF8Byte
  | three_byte_lead (b : UInt8) : UTF8Byte
  | four_byte_lead (b : UInt8) : UTF8Byte

def classifyUTF8Byte (b : UInt8) : UTF8Byte :=
  if b < 0x80 then UTF8Byte.ascii b
  else if b >= 0xC0 ∧ b < 0xE0 then UTF8Byte.two_byte_lead b
  else if b >= 0xE0 ∧ b < 0xF0 then UTF8Byte.three_byte_lead b
  else if b >= 0xF0 ∧ b < 0xF8 then UTF8Byte.four_byte_lead b
  else UTF8Byte.continuation b

def isContinuationByte (b : UInt8) : Bool :=
  b ≥ 0x80 ∧ b < 0xC0

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def validateUTF8_precond (bytes : ByteArray) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition
def validateUTF8 (bytes : ByteArray) (h_precond : validateUTF8_precond bytes) : Bool :=
  -- !benchmark @start impl
  true
  -- !benchmark @end impl

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
def isValidUTF8Sequence (bytes : ByteArray) : Prop :=
  let rec validate (i : Nat) (expected_continuations : Nat) : Prop :=
    if i ≥ bytes.size then
      expected_continuations = 0
    else
      let b := bytes[i]!
      match classifyUTF8Byte b with
      | UTF8Byte.ascii _ =>
        expected_continuations = 0 ∧ validate (i + 1) 0
      | UTF8Byte.two_byte_lead _ =>
        expected_continuations = 0 ∧ validate (i + 1) 1
      | UTF8Byte.three_byte_lead _ =>
        expected_continuations = 0 ∧ validate (i + 1) 2
      | UTF8Byte.four_byte_lead _ =>
        expected_continuations = 0 ∧ validate (i + 1) 3
      | UTF8Byte.continuation _ =>
        if expected_continuations > 0 then
          validate (i + 1) (expected_continuations - 1)
        else
          False
  validate 0 0

problem_description:
Removes the specified number of characters (Unicode code points) from the end of the string.

If `n` is greater than `s.length`, returns `""`.

Examples:
* `"red green blue".dropRight 5 = "red green"`
* `"red green blue".dropRight 11 = "red"`
* `"red green blue".dropRight 50 = ""`
formal_problem:
import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.dropRight_precond (s : String) (n : Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition
-- String.dropRight

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.dropRight_postcond (s : String) (n : Nat) (result: String) (h_precond : String.dropRight_precond s n) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  -- The result is obtained by dropping n characters from the right of s
    -- Case 1: If n >= s.length, the result is empty
    (n ≥ s.length → result = "") ∧
    -- Case 2: If n < s.length, the result has length s.length - n
    (n < s.length → result.length = s.length - n) ∧
    -- Case 3: The result is a prefix of the original string
    (n < s.length → result = s.take (s.length - n)) ∧
    -- Case 4: When n >= s.length, result is empty (redundant but explicit)
    (n ≥ s.length → result.length = 0)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- Proof content
theorem String.dropRight_postcond_satisfied (s: String) (n: Nat) (h_precond : String.dropRight_precond s n) :

Internal implementation of `Array.qsort`.

`qpartition as lt lo hi hlo hhi` returns a pair `(⟨m, h₁, h₂⟩, as')` where

- `lo ≤ m`
- `m < n`
- `∀ i, lo ≤ i → i < m → lt as[i] as[m]`
- `∀ j, m < j → j < hi → !lt as[j] as[m]`

if necessary so that the middle (pivot) element is at index `hi`.
We then iterate from `k = lo` to `k = hi`, with a pointer `i` starting at `lo`, and
swapping each element which is less than the pivot to position `i`, and then incrementing `i`.

problem_description:
Splits a string `s` on occurrences of the separator string `sep`. The default separator is `" "`.

When `sep` is empty, the result is `[s]`. When `sep` occurs in overlapping patterns, the first match
is taken. There will always be exactly `n+1` elements in the returned list if there were `n`
non-overlapping matches of `sep` in the string. The separators are not included in the returned
substrings.

Examples:
* `"here is some text ".splitOn = ["here", "is", "some", "text", ""]`
* `"here is some text ".splitOn "some" = ["here is ", " text "]`
* `"here is some text ".splitOn "" = ["here is some text "]`
* `"ababacabac".splitOn "aba" = ["", "bac", "c"]`

import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def String.splitOn_precond (s : String) (sep : optParam String " ") : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- Function definition
String.splitOn

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
-- Helper function to check if a string starts with a given prefix
def String.startsWith' (s : String) (prefix : String) : Bool :=
  s.startsWith prefix

-- Helper function to count non-overlapping occurrences of sep in s
def countNonOverlapping (s : String) (sep : String) : Nat :=
  if sep.isEmpty then 0
  else
    let rec count (pos : Nat) (acc : Nat) : Nat :=
      if h : pos ≤ s.length then
        let remaining := s.drop pos
        if remaining.startsWith sep then
          count (pos + sep.length) (acc + 1)
        else if pos < s.length then
          count (pos + 1) acc
        else
          acc
      else
        acc
    count 0 0

-- Helper function to reconstruct the original string from split result and separator
def reconstructString (parts : List String) (sep : String) : String :=
  match parts with
  | [] => ""
  | [x] => x
  | x :: xs => x ++ sep ++ reconstructString xs sep

@[reducible, simp]
def String.splitOn_postcond (s : String) (sep : optParam String " ") (result: List String) (h_precond : String.splitOn_precond (s) (sep)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  -- The result is never empty (always has at least one element)
    result ≠ [] ∧
    -- If sep is empty, result is [s]
    (sep.isEmpty → result = [s]) ∧
    -- If sep is non-empty, the number of elements equals the number of non-overlapping matches + 1
    (!sep.isEmpty → result.length = countNonOverlapping s sep + 1) ∧
    -- None of the result strings contain sep as a substring (except possibly if sep is empty)
    (!sep.isEmpty → ∀ part ∈ result, !part.contains sep) ∧
    -- Reconstructing with sep gives back the original string
    (reconstructString result sep = s)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond
